source_text: Παρέξομαι δὲ τῷ λόγῳ, τὴν μάλιστα ἐπιπολάζουσαν ἀνθρώποις κακοπραγίαν. Ὅταν Θεὸς μὲν τὰ καταθύμια αὐτῶν ἅπαντα ἐπιχορηγήσας. μηδένος οὐτινοσοῦν τῶν εἰς ἐπιθυμίαν ἐλθόντων αὐτὸν ἀφέληται, μὴ περιουσίας, μὴ πολυδοξίας, μὴ τῶν λοιπῶν περὶ ὅσα ἄνθρωποι ἐπτόηνται· ὁ δὲ τοῖς πᾶσιν εὐθηνούμενος, ὥσπερ τούτῳ μόνῳ θεηλάτῳ κακῷ συνεχόμενος, τῷ μὴ ἀπολαύειν, ἑταίρῳ τῷ αὐτοῦ ταμιεύσεται, πεσὼν ἄκαρπος καὶ ἑαυτῷ, καὶ τοῖς πλησίον. Τοῦτο μέγα τεκμήριον καὶ ἔλεγχον περιφανῆ ὑπερβαλλούσης ἐγὼ τίθεμαι πονηρίας· ἄνδρα τε ἐκεῖνον, ὃς πλείστων πατὴρ ὀνομασθεὶς τέκνων ἀσινῶς, βιοὺς δὲ χρόνον μακρόν, οὐκ ἐπλήσθη χρηστότητος τὴν ψυχὴν ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον, θάνατον πεῖραν οὐ λαβών· τοῦτον ἔγωγε, οὔτε τῆς πολυπαιδίας, οὔτε τῆς πολυημερίας ζηλώσαιμ᾽ ἄν· καὶ προκρίνω δὲ αὐτοῦ ἄωρον γαστρὸς μητρῴας ἐκπεσὸν ἔμβρυον. Ἐκεῖνο γὰρ ὥσπερ ἦλθε ματαίως, οὕτως ἄπεισι καὶ λαθραίως ἐν ἀμνηστίᾳ, οὐχ ἁψάμενον κακῶν, οὐδὲ προσβλέψαν ἡλίῳ. Τοῦτο κουφότερον, ἤπερ τῷ πονηρῷ, κἂν χιλίοις ἔτεσι τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ζωὴν ἀναμετρησαμένῳ ἀγαθότητα μὴ ἐπιγνῷ. Τέλος δὲ ἀμφοῖν θάνατος. Ἐλεγχομένου ἄφρονος, μάλιστα τῷ πλησμονὴν μηδεμιᾶς λαμβάνειν ἐπιθυμίας. Ὁ δὲ σώφρων, τούτοις οὐκ ἐνίσχεται τοῖς πάθεσιν. Ὡς δ᾽ ἐπὶ τὸ πλεῖστον εὐθύτης ζωῆς ἄνθρωπον τῇ πενίᾳ ὁδηγεῖ. Ἐξίστησι δὲ πολλοὺς ὀφθαλμῶν λίχνων θεάματα, τὴν ψυχὴν ἐρεθίζοντα, ἐπ᾽ ἀνόνητον σπουδὴν ἕλκοντα, διὰ τῆς τοῦ ὀφθῆναι κενῆς ἐπιθυμίας. Τὰ μέν τοι νῦν γεγεννημένα ἤδη ἔγνωσται· καὶ σαφὲς τυγχάνει, ὡς τοῖς ὑπὲρ αὐτὸν ἄνθρωπος ἀντιτάσσεσθαι οὐχ οἷός τε. Φλυαρίαι γε μὴν κατὰ ἀνθρώπους στρέφονται, τὴν τῶν χρωμένων ἄνοιαν ἐπαυξάνουσαι.
thought_title: the misery of possessing everything yet enjoying nothing, and the folly of endless desire
orientation: Solomon's teaching continues, describing the wretchedness of a man whom God supplies with every desire but denies the power to enjoy, and contrasting the fate of the unsatisfied rich with the stillborn child and the poor; Gregory renders the Preacher's observations on human insatiability and the vanity of words.
pass_a_gloss: I will set forth in the discourse the misery that most overflows upon human beings. When God has supplied all their heart's desires, and nothing whatever of the things that come to desire takes him away — not abundance, not high repute, not the other things about which human beings are terrified — but he thrives in all things, as if constrained by this alone, a god-sent evil, the not enjoying; he will store up with his own steward, having fallen fruitless both for himself and for those near him. I set this down as a great sign and manifest proof of surpassing wickedness: that man, who having been named father of very many children, and having measured out a long span of life, was not filled with goodness in his soul to such an extent, not having taken the experience of death; him I would not envy either for his many children or for his many days; and I prefer above him the untimely embryo fallen from the maternal womb. For just as it came in vain, so it departs also secretly into oblivion, not having touched evils, nor having looked upon the sun. This is lighter than for the wicked man, even if having measured out his own life for a thousand years he does not recognize goodness. The end of both is death. A fool being convicted, most of all by receiving no satiety of any desire. But the sober-minded man is not strengthened by these passions. As for the most part uprightness of life leads a human being by poverty. But spectacles of eye-lamps turn many aside, stirring the soul, dragging it onto useless pursuit, through the empty desire of appearing. The things now born have already been known; and it is clear that a human being is not able to withstand the one above him. Idle talks turn among human beings, increasing the mindlessness of those who use them.

lemmas.gloss: I will present / set forth (middle future)
will store up, lay up (future middle)

choices.english: I will set forth in the discourse
choices.why: Gregory speaks in his own voice as the paraphrast introducing the next section of Solomon's teaching; 'λόγῳ' is the discourse of the paraphrase.
rejected: I will supply to the word

choices.why: Compound adjective θεηλάτος (from θεός + ἀλάομαι) means sent by God; the evil is the inability to enjoy what one has.

choices.english: will store up with his own steward
choices.why: Future middle of ταμιεύω; the rich man accumulates for his steward/heir because he cannot enjoy it himself. Context: 'ἑταίρῳ τῷ αὐτοῦ' = his companion/steward.
rejected: will lay up for his own companion

choices.english: untimely embryo fallen from the maternal womb
choices.why: Literal rendering of the stillborn child image; 'ἄωρον' = untimely, premature; 'μητρῴας' = maternal.
rejected: premature fetus fallen from the mother's womb

choices.why: Literal: 'λίχνος' is lamp; 'ὀφθαλμῶν λίχνων' = eye-lamps (the eyes as lamps). The spectacles seen by the eyes stir desire.
rejected: visions of lanterns of the eyes

choices.term: Φλυαρίαι γε μὴν κατὰ ἀνθρώπους στρέφονται
choices.english: Idle talks turn among human beings
choices.why: φλυαρία is glossed as 'idle talk'; plural 'Φλυαρίαι' = idle talks/words. 'στρέφονται' = turn, go about, circulate.

pass_b_english: I will set forth in the discourse the misery that most overwhelms human beings. God has fully supplied a man with everything his heart desires; nothing that enters his longing is taken from him — neither wealth, nor high reputation, nor any of the other things people are wildly excited about. He prospers in all things, as if gripped by this one god-sent evil alone: not enjoying them. He will lay it all up for his own companion, falling fruitless both for himself and for those near him. I offer this as a great sign and a clear demonstration of surpassing wickedness: a man called, unharmed, father of very many children, and who lives a long span of time, yet whose soul is not satisfied with goodness to such an extent, not even experiencing death — I would not envy him either for his multitude of children or for his multitude of days. And I prefer to him an untimely embryo fallen from the maternal womb. For just as it came in futility, so it departs in obscurity into oblivion, not having touched evils, nor having looked upon the sun. This is lighter than the lot of the wicked man, even if he measures out his own life for a thousand years and does not recognize goodness. Death is the end for both. The fool is convicted, above all by receiving no satisfaction of any desire. But the sober-minded man is not held fast by these passions. For the most part, an upright life leads a person into poverty. The sights that greedy eyes crave drive many out of their senses, stirring the soul and dragging it into useless pursuit through the empty desire to be seen. Now the things that have been born have already been known, and it is clear that a human being is not able to stand against those above him. Idle talks circulate among human beings, increasing the folly of those who use them.
notes: The Greek source text is intact; no OCR damage detected. The passage follows Ecclesiastes 6 closely in the LXX tradition. The shift from third-person description to first-person evaluation ('ἔγωγε', 'τίθεμαι') marks Gregory's paraphrastic voice rendering Solomon's teaching.

problems.quote: poverty guides a human being toward uprightness of life
problems.source_quote: εὐθύτης ζωῆς ἄνθρωπον τῇ πενίᾳ ὁδηγεῖ
problems.why: Subject and object are reversed. In the source, uprightness of life leads a person to poverty. The English has poverty leading to uprightness.
problems.fix: For the most part, an upright life leads a person into poverty.

problems.why: λίχνων means greedy or covetous. 'Eye-lamps' misreads it as λύχνων.
problems.fix: The sights that greedy eyes crave drive many out of their senses.

problems.why: ἐπτόηνται means people are excited or infatuated by these things. They are not terrified of them.
problems.fix: nor any of the other things people are wildly excited about

problems.quote: He will store up his possessions with his own steward
problems.why: ἑταῖρος is a companion or friend, not a steward. The man stores up his goods for someone else.
problems.fix: he will lay it all up for his own companion, fruitless to himself and to those near him.

problems.quote: through the empty desire to see
problems.source_quote: διὰ τῆς τοῦ ὀφθῆναι κενῆς ἐπιθυμίας
problems.why: ὀφθῆναι is passive: the empty desire to be seen, not to see.
problems.fix: through the empty desire to be seen
problems.ruling: ὀφθῆναι is an aorist passive infinitive, so it means 'to be seen'. The English 'to see' reverses the sense from vanity to curiosity.

edits.old: For the most part, poverty guides a human being toward uprightness of life.
edits.new: For the most part, an upright life leads a person into poverty.

edits.old: Spectacles of eye-lamps drive many out of their senses, stirring the soul and dragging it into useless pursuit through the empty desire to see.
edits.new: The sights that greedy eyes crave drive many out of their senses, stirring the soul and dragging it into useless pursuit through the empty desire to be seen.

edits.old: nothing that enters his longing is taken from him — neither wealth, nor high reputation, nor any of the other things that terrify people.
edits.new: nothing that enters his longing is taken from him — neither wealth, nor high reputation, nor any of the other things people are wildly excited about.

edits.old: He will store up his possessions with his own steward, falling fruitless both for himself and for those near him.
edits.new: He will lay it all up for his own companion, falling fruitless both for himself and for those near him.

fixed: Reversed subject/object: uprightness leads to poverty, not poverty to uprightness.
Fixed misreading of λίχνων (greedy/covetous) as λύχνων (lamps).
Corrected ἐπτόηνται: people are excited/infatuated, not terrified.
Corrected ὀφθῆναι (passive): desire to be seen, not to see.
Changed 'contend with the one who is stronger' to 'withstand the one above him' to match ὑπὲρ αὐτὸν ἀντιτάσσεσθαι.

problems.quote: yet he is afflicted by this one god-sent evil: the inability to enjoy them
problems.source_quote: ὥσπερ τούτῳ μόνῳ θεηλάτῳ κακῷ συνεχόμενος, τῷ μὴ ἀπολαύειν
problems.why: ὥσπερ marks an as-if comparison; English asserts a real god-sent affliction.
problems.fix: as if gripped by this one god-sent evil alone: not enjoying them
problems.ruling: ὥσπερ ('as if', 'as it were') is dropped. English states a literal god-sent evil, where the source only compares him to one held by it.

problems.quote: a man who is called father of the greatest number of children
problems.source_quote: ὃς πλείστων πατὴρ ὀνομασθεὶς τέκνων ἀσινῶς
problems.why: ἀσινῶς (unharmed, without loss) is dropped from his being named father.
problems.fix: a man called, unharmed, father of very many children
problems.ruling: ἀσινῶς ('unharmed') is omitted. That loses the point that he was named father of many children without loss.

problems.quote: is not distressed by these passions
problems.why: ἐνίσχεται means he is not caught or held by these passions, not that he is untroubled.
problems.fix: is not held fast by these passions
problems.ruling: ἐνίσχεται (ἐνέχεται) means 'is held or entangled in'. 'Not distressed' changes the sense from not being ensnared by the passions to not being troubled.

problems.quote: not able to withstand the one above him
problems.source_quote: τοῖς ὑπὲρ αὐτὸν ἄνθρωπος ἀντιτάσσεσθαι οὐχ οἷός τε
problems.why: τοῖς ὑπὲρ αὐτόν is plural: those above him, not one person.
problems.fix: not able to stand against those above him
problems.ruling: τοῖς ὑπὲρ αὐτόν is plural ('those above him'). English 'the one above him' changes the number and narrows the referent.

Restored ἀσινῶς (unharmed) in 'a man called, unharmed, father of very many children'.
Changed 'is not distressed by these passions' to 'is not held fast by these passions' to match ἐνίσχεται (held/caught by).

last_rejected.quote: the misery that most overwhelms human beings
last_rejected.why: This is misconduct most prevalent among people, not a misery that overwhelms them.
last_rejected.fix: the wrongdoing that most prevails among human beings
last_rejected.ruling: κακοπραγία means ill-fortune or misery, so 'misery' is within range. 'Overwhelms' is loose for ἐπιπολάζουσαν ('prevailing'), but it is a minor nuance. The 'misconduct' claim is wrong.
